newsitem.title: FRANCE: French employers' chief hopes Britain joins EMU.
newsitem.headline: French employers' chief hopes Britain joins EMU.

text.p: The chairman of France's employers' federation CNPF said on Tuesday he hoped Britain, Spain and Italy would join the planned European monetary union, saying it would offset Germany's powerful influence on the new currency.
"The dangers of a long-lasting isolation of three economic powers -- Italy, Spain and Britain -- should be avoided," Jean Gandois told the influential lobby group's annual meeting.
With a core of just Germany, France, Benelux countries and Austria, "the role of the mark (in the new euro currency) would be too important," Gandois said.
French employers have long been wary of an overly strong euro, fearing it would undercut exports, and see a wide-based currency union as protection.
Gandois, whose group has championed a single currency, also said business was worried about competitive devaluations by those outside the monetary union.
President Jacques Chirac complained earlier this year that French industry had suffered from devaluations of the lira, pound and the peseta.

Britain has so far kept its options open on joining the single currency, due to start on January 1, 1999, but Italy and Spain, long seen as laggards in meeting the tough qualifications, are striving to get their finances in order.
Gandois rejected government charges that business was failing to do its part cut record 12.6 percent unemployment.
"The only thing that will lower unemployment is strong enough (economic) growth and not having regulations and bureacracy discouraging hiring," he said.
